title: Equal trace aligns planar design objectives but does not make greedy selection exact
problem: Determine whether equal information capacity per source removes the arbitrary failure of E-greedy selection in R25.
failure: Equal trace does not make greedy selection optimal, even with two choices and strictly positive definite groups. Conversely, the unequal-trace arbitrary-failure example must not be transferred unchanged to the equal-trace model.
correction: Represent each planar equal-trace matrix by its traceless imbalance vector. E, D and inverse-trace A rankings coincide at fixed cardinality. With an isotropic positive baseline and budget two, greedy achieves at least one quarter of optimal E gain above baseline; an explicit rational family approaches the quarter ratio.
transfer: Recheck guarantees when resource constraints change. Separate equal aggregate capacity from directional distribution, and use exact small-instance comparisons plus a worst-case construction.
limits: Two-dimensional independent additive PSD information, equal trace and equal group costs; isotropic baseline for the two-choice bound. 85320 exact disk-grid triple comparisons and eight rational sharp-family examples. Common trace grows across sharpness instances. No larger-budget, arbitrary baseline ratio, correlated-noise, physical, organizational, novelty or independent validation claim.
author: TOTO
